subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Condensers: Completing the Steam Cycle
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Condensers: Completing the Steam Cycle.

hook.text: After steam does its work, it must become water again. The condenser closes the loop.

buildup.text: A condenser cools exhaust steam back into liquid water. Cool water or air flows past tubes carrying the steam.

discovery.text: Condensing creates a vacuum that pulls steam through the turbine faster. Lower back-pressure means more power.

twist.text: Power plants near rivers use river water for cooling. That's why nuclear plants are always near water sources.

climax.text: Cooling towers are giant condensers. The white clouds rising from power plants are just evaporating water.

punchline.text: Steam out, water back. The cycle never ends.

quiz.question: Why does condensing exhaust steam improve turbine efficiency?
options: It heats the incoming steam to a higher temperature
It creates a vacuum that reduces back-pressure on the turbine
It removes impurities that would damage the turbine blades
